summary:
Hitting is the category to lean on today across the board — R1, R2, and R3 all show it running hot at 62% over the last 14 days (n=16), with R2 posting the biggest edge at +13.1pts over its 49% season baseline and R3 close behind at +12.9pts. Bullpen_fatigue is the other live trend, hot in all four ratings (+9.5 to +10.3pts, with R1-R3 riding 3-game win streaks in that category). Starting pitcher ratings remain the fade across the board — every rating is cold on SP by double digits (-15 to -17.5pts) despite a paradoxical 3W streak, so treat any pick that leans heavily on SP grades with suspicion today unless hitting or bullpen_fatigue confirms it. R4's bullpen read is also cold at -10.5pts with a 3L streak, so don't trust R4 bullpen-driven plays even though its season number (54%) looks fine in isolation.

On the board today, prioritize games where hitting and bullpen_fatigue line up — that's the strongest live signal intersection, especially layered onto trends+runs or trends+bullpen combos, which sit at 57.1% and 56.7% season-wide and should be the first screen for agreement. R2 is the rating to trust most right now: it's 4-0 (+4.0u) over the last 7 days and 5-2 (+2.0u) over 14 on strong plays, clearly outpacing R4's ice-cold 0-2 (-2.0u) stretch — fade R4 strong plays until that cools off. If any of today's slate features LAD, BOS, or TBR as the model's side, lean in hard — LAD strong plays are hitting 80% (+27.0u), BOS 76% (+19.0u), and TBR 70% (+21.0u), all best-in-class team trust levels. Conversely, if NYY shows up as today's pick, downgrade confidence regardless of rating — strong plays on NYY are 39% (-4.0u), the weakest team on the board by a wide margin.
